content.value_statement: Autonomous workflows often fail because errors, costs, and context grow across steps. This skill provides patterns for bounded planning, execution, reflection, recovery, and human approval.
actual_capabilities: Explains ReAct, Plan-Execute, and reflection loops with guidance for selecting each pattern.
Demonstrates LangGraph checkpointing, human interrupts, state recovery, and time-travel debugging.
Defines guardrails for action allowlists, approvals, costs, step limits, and rollback.
Identifies production risks from compounding errors, context growth, fabricated data, permissions, and integration failures.
Provides validation checks for timeouts, durable memory, thread identifiers, output validation, and structured responses.
limitations: Provides guidance and illustrative snippets, not an executable package or deployable agent.
Does not configure infrastructure, credentials, databases, or external services.
Framework APIs and model references may require verification against current vendor documentation.
Cannot guarantee reliability; each implementation needs domain tests, monitoring, and security review.

use_cases.title: Design a Task Agent
use_cases.description: Select an agent loop, define completion criteria, and add bounded execution for a focused application workflow.
use_cases.target_user: Application developers building their first autonomous workflow

use_cases.title: Harden Agent Operations
use_cases.description: Add checkpoints, cost limits, observability, retries, approvals, and rollback to an existing agent.
use_cases.target_user: Platform engineers preparing agents for production

use_cases.title: Assess Product Risk
use_cases.description: Evaluate proposed automation against reliability, permission, integration, context, and human oversight requirements.
use_cases.target_user: AI product leads reviewing autonomous features

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Agent Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: For {workflow}, compare ReAct, Plan-Execute, and reflection. Recommend one pattern and explain required tools, limits, completion criteria, and human approval points.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when selecting a basic architecture for a new workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Bounded Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an autonomous agent for {goal}. Define state, step limits, allowed actions, cost limits, completion criteria, escalation rules, and failure handling.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when turning a clear goal into a constrained agent design.

prompt_templates.title: Review Agent Reliability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent design: {design}. Identify compounding failures, missing validation, context growth, weak observability, unsafe permissions, and recovery gaps. Prioritize the fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before moving an agent prototype toward production.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production architecture for {domain} using {framework}. Include checkpointing, idempotency, human interrupts, evaluation, audit logging, rollback, cost controls, and staged deployment. State assumptions and residual risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an advanced system spanning models, tools, state, and external integrations.

output_examples.input: Design a customer refund agent with access to order records and payment tools.
output: Pattern: Plan-Execute with approval before payment changes.
Controls: Read-only order access, refund limits, explicit completion criteria, and a ten-step maximum.
Recovery: Checkpoint before payment calls, use idempotency keys, and escalate ambiguous cases.

output_examples.input: Review an agent that researches vendors, selects one, and sends a purchase order.
output: Primary risk: The agent combines recommendation and irreversible execution without independent approval.
Required changes: Separate research from purchasing, validate evidence, restrict spending, and require a human signature.
Monitoring: Record each source, decision, tool call, cost, and authorization.

output_examples.input: Compare ReAct and reflection for improving technical support answers.
output_examples.output: Use ReAct when the agent must gather account facts through tools. Add bounded reflection when answer quality needs evaluation against explicit support criteria.

best_practices: Set explicit step, cost, time, permission, and completion boundaries before enabling tools.
Checkpoint state and require human approval before irreversible or high-impact actions.
Validate outputs against evidence and monitor every decision, tool call, failure, and recovery.
anti_patterns: Do not grant broad permissions to an agent whose goals or success criteria are ambiguous.
Do not allow unbounded loops, context growth, retries, or API spending.
Do not treat model output as verified truth or execute uncertain results automatically.

faq.question: What agent patterns does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers ReAct, Plan-Execute, reflection, guardrailed autonomy, durable execution, and human approval patterns.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete agent application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and illustrative examples that require implementation, testing, and environment-specific configuration.

faq.question: Which frameworks appear in the guidance?
faq.answer: The skill discusses LangGraph, LangChain, AutoGPT, CrewAI, the Claude Agent SDK, and related evaluation and tracing tools.

faq.question: How does the skill limit dangerous actions?
faq.answer: It recommends least privilege, action allowlists, explicit approvals, dry runs, audit logs, checkpoints, and rollback.

faq.question: How does it address long-running tasks?
faq.answer: It recommends durable checkpoints, unique thread identifiers, context compaction, cost tracking, timeouts, and recovery from saved state.

faq.question: Can these examples be used without review?
faq.answer: No. Verify framework APIs, supply secure configuration, test adversarial cases, and review permissions before production use.
